passages.title: A Day at the Science Fair
text: Last Saturday, my friend Lintang and I took part in the regional science fair at Universitas Negeri Semarang. We had worked on our project for almost three months. It was a simple water filter made from sand, charcoal, and old plastic bottles.

We left home at 5.30 a.m. because the registration desk opened at seven. When we arrived, the hall was already full of students setting up their tables. We found our spot, put up our poster, and filled two bottles with muddy water from a pond near my house.

At about nine o'clock, the first judge came to our table. She was a professor of environmental engineering. I was so nervous that I forgot the first sentence of our presentation. Luckily, Lintang started talking and I soon remembered what to say. We poured the muddy water into the filter, and after a few minutes clear water came out at the bottom. The professor looked impressed, but she asked a difficult question: was the water safe to drink? We admitted that we had not tested it for bacteria.
In the afternoon, we walked around the hall and looked at other projects. My favourite was a solar-powered dryer for fish made by students from Jepara.

At four o'clock, the results were announced. We did not win a prize, but our project received a special note from the judges for using recycled materials. On the way home, Lintang and I were already talking about adding a bacteria test next year. It was a tiring day, but I learned that a good project always leads to new questions.

passages.title: My First Week as a Barista
text: During the school holiday in July, I worked as a part-time barista at Kopi Pagi, a small coffee shop near the train station in Bandung. I had always wanted to learn how to make coffee professionally, so I was very excited when the owner, Mas Bayu, accepted my application.

On my first day, I did not touch the coffee machine at all. Mas Bayu asked me to clean the tables, wash cups, and watch how the senior barista, Kak Sinta, served customers. I felt a little bored, but by the end of the day I had memorized the whole menu.

On the second and third days, Kak Sinta taught me how to grind the beans and how to use the espresso machine. My first few cups were terrible. Some were too bitter and others were too weak. Kak Sinta told me to measure the coffee carefully and to time every shot. By Wednesday afternoon, my espresso finally tasted right.

The most stressful moment came on Friday morning. A group of twenty office workers came in at the same time, and Kak Sinta was on her break. I took the orders one by one, wrote them on cups, and worked as fast as I could. Two drinks were wrong, but I apologized and made them again. When Kak Sinta came back, she smiled and said I had handled the rush well.
At the end of the week, Mas Bayu gave me my first pay and a bag of coffee beans. I was tired, but I felt proud. That week taught me that every skill takes patience and practice.

passages.title: The Day the Volcano Woke Up
text: On the night of 13 February 2014, Mount Kelud in East Java erupted. The following account was written by Pak Darmo, a farmer from a village about ten kilometres from the crater.

"At around half past nine that evening, the village head went from house to house and told us to leave. The government had raised the alert to the highest level. We put our documents and some clothes in a bag and drove our motorbikes to a school building in the next district, where many families were already staying.

Shortly before eleven, we heard a loud explosion, like thunder that did not stop. A few minutes later, small stones and sand began to fall on the roof of the school. By morning, everything outside was grey. The ash was about ten centimetres thick, and the air smelled of sulphur.

We stayed at the school for nine days. Volunteers brought rice, water, and masks. Doctors checked the children and old people every morning. When we were finally allowed to go home, many roofs had fallen in because of the heavy ash, and my pineapple field was completely covered.

It took my neighbours and me more than two months to clean our houses and fields. The first harvest after the eruption was small, but the next one was surprisingly good. Some people say the ash makes the soil rich again. I am just thankful that everyone in our village is safe."

passages.title: The Charity Run
text: Last month, my school organised a five-kilometre charity run to raise money for a children's hospital in our city. I was not a good runner, but my best friend Dewi persuaded me to register. 'It's for a good cause,' she said, 'and we can walk if we get tired.'

The run started at seven o'clock on Sunday morning in front of the city hall. More than two hundred people were waiting at the starting line, including teachers, parents, and even a few grandparents. A teacher blew a whistle, and everyone began to move. During the first kilometre, I kept up with Dewi easily. The streets were closed to traffic, and people along the road were clapping and shouting encouragement.

Halfway through, I started to feel pain in my side, and my legs became heavy. I slowed down, and Dewi stayed with me. Then, near the third kilometre, I stepped on a loose stone and twisted my ankle. I sat down on the pavement, ready to give up. A volunteer in an orange vest hurried over, gave me some water, and put a cold pack on my ankle. After ten minutes, I decided to try walking.

Dewi and I walked the last two kilometres together. People we had never met cheered for us as if we were running at the front. When we finally crossed the finish line, one hour and ten minutes had passed, which was the slowest time of all our classmates. Still, I was proud. That afternoon, the school announced that the run had collected more than forty million rupiah.

questions.question: What was the writer's science project?

options.C: A test for bacteria in pond water
options.D: A water filter made from recycled materials

questions.explanation: Paragraf 1: a simple water filter made from sand, charcoal, and old plastic bottles. Pengering ikan tenaga surya adalah proyek siswa Jepara.

questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct order of events?

options.A: They presented to the judge → they set up their table → they visited other projects
options.B: The results were announced → they presented to the judge → they went home
options.C: They visited other projects → they set up their table → the results were announced
options.D: They set up their table → they presented to the judge → they visited other projects

questions.explanation: Urutan peristiwa: tiba dan memasang poster (paragraf 2), presentasi kepada juri sekitar pukul 09.00 (paragraf 3), berkeliling melihat proyek lain pada siang hari (paragraf 4), lalu pengumuman pukul 16.00.

questions.question: What problem did the professor point out about the project?

options.A: The filter could not make the water clear.
options.B: The poster did not explain the project well.
options.C: The water had not been tested for bacteria.
options.D: The project used too much charcoal.

questions.explanation: Profesor bertanya apakah airnya aman diminum, dan mereka mengakui we had not tested it for bacteria.

questions.question: What can we learn about Lintang from the text?

options.A: She helped the writer when the writer forgot the presentation.
options.B: She was more nervous than the writer.
options.C: She disagreed with the judges' decision.
options.D: She wanted to stop working on the project.

questions.explanation: Saat penulis lupa kalimat pembuka, Lintang started talking and I soon remembered what to say. Lintang juga ikut merencanakan uji bakteri tahun depan, jadi ia tidak ingin berhenti.

questions.question: What is the function of the last paragraph?

options.A: To introduce the participants and the place
options.B: To describe the most exciting event of the day
options.C: To give the result and the writer's personal comment
options.D: To explain how the water filter works

questions.explanation: Struktur recount: paragraf terakhir adalah reorientation yang berisi hasil akhir (tidak menang, tetapi mendapat catatan khusus) dan kesan atau pelajaran penulis.

questions.question: What did the writer do on the first day at work?

options.B: Ground coffee beans with Kak Sinta
options.D: Cleaned tables, washed cups, and watched the senior barista

questions.explanation: Paragraf 2: I did not touch the coffee machine at all; ia membersihkan meja, mencuci gelas, dan memperhatikan Kak Sinta.

questions.question: Why did the writer's first cups of coffee taste bad?

options.C: The writer did not measure and time the coffee carefully.
options.D: Kak Sinta gave the writer the wrong recipe.

questions.explanation: Kak Sinta menyarankan to measure the coffee carefully and to time every shot. Setelah itu kopinya terasa pas, jadi masalahnya ada di takaran dan waktu.

questions.question:
Which words best describe the writer during the Friday morning rush?
(1) Calm and responsible
(2) Careless and rude
(3) Hard-working and polite
(4) Lazy and dependent on others
questions.explanation: Penulis mencatat pesanan satu per satu dan bekerja secepat mungkin (bertanggung jawab, pekerja keras), serta meminta maaf dan membuat ulang minuman yang salah (sopan). Kak Sinta juga menilai ia handled the rush well.

questions.question: The phrase handled the rush in paragraph 4 means ....

options.A: dealt successfully with a busy period
options.C: refused to serve too many people
options.D: asked for help during the break

questions.explanation: Rush di sini berarti saat ramai pelanggan datang bersamaan; handle berarti menangani. Jadi penulis berhasil menangani saat sibuk.

questions.question: What is the main message of the text?

options.A: Learning a new skill takes patience and practice.
options.B: Working in a coffee shop is very easy.
options.C: Customers in Bandung prefer strong coffee.
options.D: Senior workers should not take breaks.

questions.explanation: Kalimat terakhir menyatakan pesan secara langsung: every skill takes patience and practice.

questions.question: Where did Pak Darmo's family stay after leaving the village?

options.B: At a hospital in the city
options.C: In a tent near the pineapple field
options.D: At a school building in the next district

questions.explanation: drove our motorbikes to a school building in the next district.

questions.question:
Decide whether each event happened before or after the eruption, according to Pak Darmo's account.
(1) The village head told people to leave.
(2) Volunteers brought rice, water, and masks.

options.B: (1) Before the eruption; (2) After the eruption; (3) Before the eruption
options.C: (1) Before the eruption; (2) After the eruption; (3) After the eruption

questions.explanation: Kepala desa datang sekitar pukul 21.30 dan keluarga langsung mengungsi; ledakan terjadi sebelum pukul 23.00. Relawan membawa bantuan selama sembilan hari di pengungsian setelah letusan.

questions.question: Why had many roofs fallen in when the villagers returned home?

options.A: Strong earthquakes had shaken the houses.
options.B: The ash on the roofs was too heavy.
options.C: Hot lava had flowed into the village.

questions.explanation: many roofs had fallen in because of the heavy ash. Teks tidak menyebut gempa atau lava yang masuk desa.

questions.question: Pak Darmo says Some people say the ash makes the soil rich again. Which statement best evaluates this sentence?

options.A: It is a fact that Pak Darmo has proven with scientific tests.
options.B: It is a belief of other people that seems to match his good second harvest.
options.C: It is Pak Darmo's own strong opinion that he wants readers to accept.
options.D: It is false because his first harvest after the eruption was small.

questions.explanation: Kalimat diawali Some people say, jadi berupa pendapat orang lain, bukan hasil uji. Panen kedua yang surprisingly good tampak mendukungnya, tetapi belum membuktikannya. Panen pertama yang kecil tidak menjadikannya salah.

questions.question: What does Pak Darmo feel most at the end of the account?

options.C: Afraid of living near the volcano

questions.explanation: I am just thankful that everyone in our village is safe.

questions.question: Why did the writer join the charity run?

options.A: Dewi persuaded the writer to register for a good cause.
options.B: The writer was a skilled runner who wanted to win.
options.C: The school required every student to take part.
options.D: The writer wanted to meet the children at the hospital.

questions.explanation: Paragraf 1: penulis bukan pelari yang baik, tetapi Dewi membujuknya mendaftar karena acara itu untuk tujuan yang baik (It's for a good cause).

questions.question: Where did the run start?

options.C: In front of the city hall

questions.explanation: Paragraf 2: The run started at seven o'clock on Sunday morning in front of the city hall. Rumah sakit anak hanyalah penerima dana yang terkumpul.

questions.question:
Which of the following shows the correct order of events?
(1) A volunteer put a cold pack on the writer's ankle.
(2) The writer twisted an ankle.
(3) The run started.
(4) The writer crossed the finish line.
questions.explanation: Urutan peristiwa (recount): lomba dimulai (3), penulis terkilir di dekat kilometer ketiga (2), relawan memberi kompres dingin (1), lalu penulis mencapai garis akhir (4).

questions.question: How did the writer feel after crossing the finish line?

options.A: Embarrassed because the other classmates had finished earlier
options.B: Proud, even though the finishing time was slow
options.C: Angry with the volunteer who had delayed the run
options.D: Worried because the ankle was badly injured

questions.explanation: Paragraf 4: waktu mereka paling lambat di antara teman sekelas, Still, I was proud. Kata still menunjukkan bahwa rasa bangga tetap ada meskipun waktunya lambat.

questions.question: In paragraph 4, the writer says that strangers cheered as if we were running at the front. This suggests that the crowd ....

options.A: mistook the writer and Dewi for the winners
options.B: did not realise that the two friends were last
options.C: wanted the writer to finish the run faster
options.D: supported every runner, not only the fastest ones

questions.explanation: Frasa as if menunjukkan perbandingan: sorakan untuk mereka sama meriahnya dengan untuk pelari terdepan. Artinya penonton menyemangati semua peserta. Penonton tidak salah mengira penulis sebagai pemenang.
